summary:
Democrats are projected to regain control of both the House of Representatives and the Senate in the US midterm elections, a major setback for President Donald Trump. Economic concerns, including high oil prices, tariffs and mounting debt, played a key role in the result. Democrats can now pass legislation, but they lack the two-thirds majority needed to override Trump's veto. Elon Musk, by far the largest individual donor ever, gave over $440 million to support Republicans in an election that cost nearly $12 billion, the most expensive on record.

The Bank of England raised interest rates to 4% for the first time in more than three years, to combat rising inflation as the Iran war keeps energy costs high. The decision came a week after the budget. In France, five unions joined a national day of action on Thursday, with more than 220 demonstrations expected against the rising cost of living. Authorities deployed about 70,000 police and security officers across the country.

Fifteen flights across Europe have received bomb threats so far today, and some were forced to divert, with jet fighters scrambled. Planes linked to Italy and France landed safely, and no explosives have been found. In Hong Kong, democracy activist Joshua Wong, 30, was sentenced on Thursday to 10 more years in jail for colluding with foreign forces under the national security law.

headlines.title: Democrats take control of Congress in US midterm elections
headlines.summary: Democrats were projected to regain control of both the House and the Senate, a major setback for President Donald Trump. They can pass legislation but lack the two-thirds majority needed to override a presidential veto.

headlines.title: Bank of England raises interest rates to 4%
headlines.summary: The Bank of England raised rates to 4%, its first increase in more than three years, to combat rising inflation. It said the Iran war continues to drive up energy costs, and the decision came a week after the budget.

headlines.title: French unions launch national day of strikes and protests
headlines.summary: Five unions joined more than 220 demonstrations expected on Thursday, escalating weeks of protests against the rising cost of living. Authorities deployed about 70,000 police and security officers across the country.

headlines.title: Bomb threats divert flights across Europe; no explosives found
headlines.summary: Fifteen flights across Europe have received bomb threats so far today, and some were forced to divert. Jet fighters were scrambled, and planes linked to Italy and France landed safely, with no explosives found.

headlines.title: Joshua Wong sentenced to 10 more years in prison
headlines.summary: Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong, 30, was sentenced on Thursday to 10 more years in jail for colluding with foreign forces. It is the second time he has been penalised under the national security law.

headlines.title: South Africans vote in local elections amid failing services
headlines.summary: South Africans voted on Wednesday, November 4, in local elections in which nearly 30 million people were eligible. Corruption, failing infrastructure and water outages are key issues, and the ANC is expected to get less than a third of the vote.

headlines.title: Building collapse in Old Delhi leaves several feared trapped
headlines.summary: A building collapsed in Chawri Bazar in Old Delhi, and rescue operations are ongoing. Several people are feared trapped, and residents said they learned of the collapse from ambulance sirens and cries for help.

headlines.title: Israeli president begins consultations on forming new government
headlines.summary: President Isaac Herzog accepted the certified results of last week's parliamentary elections as legally binding on Wednesday. He began consultations with party representatives on forming a new government after an inconclusive vote.
